english: Brother, our chief is soft and has grown weary. He sits at the feast. He was strong and had great fame. Now the tribe seeks a new leader. Whom do we choose? You are known, and the mighty follow you. I do not speak against him. I will tell (reckon with) our mother.

Chief, I have seen a raiding band at the ford. How many men did you see? I saw a hundred men and many horses. Did they see you? They did not see me. They are hiding in the tall grass. Your eyes are good. Now gather the village and the warriors at a run. Do we fight at the river? We fight. Few men protect against many.
uncertain: h₂én before wikṓmes read as an affirmative particle

english: You went to the enemies' settlement at night. What then did you see? I saw their king. With a great voice he counselled that when the moon is full we cross the river. How many warriors are with them? They are more than our men. Now we do not wait. Gather the warriors and send the women across. Now I go to the chief.

Lady, you went to the settlement. What did the elders say? Do they honour the strangers? The eldest spoke; their women and children are few (they gird/... kénkonti unclear). What did the mighty say? They said: the stranger is an enemy. What did their leader say? Once our fathers were strangers. Now the leader's tribe gave land by the river. The tribe did well.

Now do we cross the river or stay for the winter? The water is deep now. If we cross, the children sink in the water. The herd follows us. If we stay, it overtakes us. Let warriors stand at the ford and women and children sit in the wagons. The cold comes soon. Now we stay the winter and they will protect us.

How many cattle do we give as blood-price to the dead man's kin? A man's price is a hundred cows. Our herd is not great. Now give seven oxen and a foal. And the mighty will herd their sheep for a year. Will his kin keep the peace? They swore an oath in council. They do not break it. Now we drive them (the cattle) in the morning.
